---
title: "Methods Summary"
description: "Synopsis of the ontology-guided qualitative thematic analysis methodology"
---

# Data Analysis

## Ontology-Centric Data Preparation

A hierarchical ontology was developed to organise qualitative evidence from the scoping review literature. The ontology was structured under four conceptual domains: problem definition, resilience mechanisms, resolution pathways, and theoretical frameworks. Each evidence excerpt was assigned to exactly one ontology node. This assignment grounded all downstream coding and thematic aggregation within a defined semantic scope. The hierarchical structure was preserved throughout the computational analysis.

## Knowledge Graph Formation

Keywords were extracted from each excerpt using KeyBERT with Maximal Marginal Relevance. All excerpts and keywords were encoded into vectors using sentence-transformer all-MiniLM-L6-v2. A BM25 lexical index complemented semantic similarity with exact-term matching. A knowledge graph captured relationships among the ontology, codes, themes, and interpretations. The graph was updated incrementally, with only affected branches requiring recomputation.

## Sequential Analysis Pipeline

The thematic analysis followed a ten-stage pipeline alternating between inference and validation. Candidate codes were generated by grouping conceptually similar excerpts within each ontology node. After author review, approved codes were aggregated into broader themes. Approved themes were synthesised into cross-cutting interpretations across multiple ontology branches. Only ontology branches with pending changes were reprocessed during iterative cycles.

## Model Integration

Two models formed the computational core: a sentence-transformer and a large language model. The sentence-transformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) produced vector embeddings for all textual content. A large language model (Groq API) generated codes, themes, and interpretations. Each batch query included analytical rules, examples, and ontology context. This approach grounded outputs within the existing knowledge structure without fine-tuning.

## Inference Stages

Inference items were grouped by ontology node or clustered by embedding similarity. Three prompt templates governed code, theme, and interpretation generation. Network errors triggered automatic retries with exponential backoff. Responses were parsed and validated against structured schemas before acceptance. Each inference stage depended on completion of the preceding validation stage.

## Constraint Validation and Output

Three structural rules governed the analytical framework. Each code belonged to exactly one theme. Each theme grouped multiple codes from the same ontology node. Each interpretation spanned a connected region of the ontology hierarchy. These constraints were enforced during inference, review, and database operation.

## Human-in-the-Loop Validation

The LLM sequentially generated initial codes, themes, and interpretations from the evidence. After each generation stage, one author (AL) validated the outputs against the original source excerpts before the next stage proceeded. Initial generations could be accepted, modified, or rejected based on the author's judgment. This interleaved workflow ensured each analytical layer was grounded before the next was produced. The author maintained full interpretive control throughout the analysis.
